title: Refined but Poor
synopsis: Spending habits vary quite a bit across generations in China. Learn about the “refined but poor” phenomenon.

fullText.simplified:
精致穷

    每种语言都会随着经济和社会的发展出现新词。而在互联网迅速普及的今天，一些网络词汇应运而生，其中不乏初听有些匪夷所思的词汇。例如：精致穷。翻开字典查阅词义你就会发现这个词语的奇异之处。精致：1，精巧、细致；2，有情致、美丽。穷就很好理解了：没有钱。这样一个褒义一个贬义的两个词语奇异地组成了一个新词，就不得不让人惊奇了。
    那么精致穷到底指代了什么样的语义呢？这就要从当今中国社会背景说起了。
    中国人历来热衷储蓄，习惯居安思危，至今居民储蓄率仍高居世界首位。然而近年来，中国人的居民储蓄率正逐渐下降，这一点在青年群体中表现尤其明显。更有不少90后自嘲“四大皆空”，即支付宝空、微信空、银行卡空、钱包空。这并不是空口无凭地自我解嘲，据调查数据显示：30%的90后是“月光族”，没有余钱用于储蓄。他们将大部分收入用于消费，其中不乏高端消费，如数码产品、奢侈品等。这些消费习惯在外表现为：年轻人们普遍光鲜亮丽，然而细探家底，手无存粮的大有人在。为了追求精致的生活，大量消费或提前消费导致自己变穷，这就是所谓的“精致穷”了。
    老一辈中国人对这种消费观念普遍持反对态度。他们认为这种消费观念是寅吃卯粮，会降低个人的抗风险能力。而年轻人的想法则更五花八门：一些人认为年轻就该享受青春，不必过度杞人忧天；一些人认为储蓄的收益率过低，把钱存进银行等于贬值，不如进行消费更划算；一些人则认为应该在年轻的时候进行自我投资，可以把储蓄计划推迟几年。双方各执一词，在没有危害社会的前提下，我们都无需过多评判。
    然而一些其他关于精致穷的社会现象却值得关注。一部分人在追求精致生活的过程中，过度提前消费，超出了自身的承受能力，造成了严重后果，这样的事情屡见报端。如很多大学生通过网贷，购买昂贵的电子产品或者名牌服饰，无力偿还，毕业前因为个人征信受损影响求职后才和父母沟通。更有甚者，因为超出家庭承担限度而自杀。
    这些悲剧让人不得不警惕，我们该如何界定合理的欲望、健康的消费观念？
    近年来，越来越多的人开始批判“消费主义的陷阱”，这是人们对过度消费的反思，也是一种探索和寻求。也许终有一天，我们能找到合理享受生活和对抗未知风险的平衡点。
fullText.traditional:
精緻窮

    每種語言都會隨著經濟和社會的發展出現新詞。而在互聯網迅速普及的今天，一些網絡詞彙應運而生，其中不乏初聽有些匪夷所思的詞彙。例如：精緻窮。翻開字典查閱詞義你就會發現這個詞語的奇異之處。精緻：1，精巧、細緻；2，有情致、美麗。窮就很好理解了：沒有錢。這樣一個褒義一個貶義的兩個詞語奇異地組成了一個新詞，就不得不讓人驚奇了。
    那麼精緻窮到底指代了什麼樣的語義呢？這就要從當今中國社會背景說起了。
    中國人歷來熱衷儲蓄，習慣居安思危，至今居民儲蓄率仍高居世界首位。然而近年來，中國人的居民儲蓄率正逐漸下降，這一點在青年群體中表現尤其明顯。更有不少90後自嘲“四大皆空”，即支付寶空、微信空、銀行卡空、錢包空。這並不是空口無憑地自我解嘲，據調查數據顯示：30%的90後是“月光族”，沒有餘錢用于儲蓄。他們將大部分收入用于消費，其中不乏高端消費，如數碼產品、奢侈品等。這些消費習慣在外表現為：年輕人們普遍光鮮亮麗，然而細探家底，手無存糧的大有人在。為了追求精緻的生活，大量消費或提前消費導致自己變窮，這就是所謂的“精緻窮”了。
    老一輩中國人對這種消費觀念普遍持反對態度。他們認為這種消費觀念是寅吃卯糧，會降低個人的抗風險能力。而年輕人的想法則更五花八門：一些人認為年輕就該享受青春，不必過度杞人憂天；一些人認為儲蓄的收益率過低，把錢存進銀行等於貶值，不如進行消費更划算；一些人則認為應該在年輕的時候進行自我投資，可以把儲蓄計劃推遲幾年。雙方各執一詞，在沒有危害社會的前提下，我們都無需過多評判。
    然而一些其他關於精緻窮的社會現象卻值得關注。一部分人在追求精緻生活的過程中，過度提前消費，超出了自身的承受能力，造成了嚴重後果，這樣的事情屢見報端。如很多大學生通過網貸，購買昂貴的電子產品或者名牌服飾，無力償還，畢業前因為個人徵信受損影響求職後才和父母溝通。更有甚者，因為超出家庭承擔限度而自殺。
    這些悲劇讓人不得不警惕，我們該如何界定合理的慾望、健康的消費觀念？
    近年來，越來越多的人開始批判“消費主義的陷阱”，這是人們對過度消費的反思，也是一種探索和尋求。也許終有一天，我們能找到合理享受生活和對抗未知風險的平衡點。

raw.synopsis: Spending habits vary quite a bit across generations in China. Learn about the “refined but poor” phenomenon.
sentence_translations: Refined but Poor
Every language sees the emergence of new terms following economic and social development.
And today, in an age where the internet is rapidly spreading, some online terms have risen to the occasion.
Of these, there are many terms that sound somewhat inconceivable at first.
For example: “refined but poor”.
If you open up a dictionary and look at the meanings of the words, you will find out why this term is so strange.
Jingzhi: 1. exquisite, delicate; 2. appealing, beautiful
Qiong is very easy to understand: having no money.
This bizarre formation of two words, one positive and one negative in meaning, into a new term will surprise people.
So, exactly what sort of meaning does “refined but poor” refer to?
We’ll have to start with the context of today’s Chinese society.
Chinese people have always been keen savers and are accustomed to preparing for emergencies.
Today, China’s household savings rate remains at the top of the global leaderboard.
Yet in recent years, China’s household savings rate has been gradually declining, ..
.. and this is especially noticeable among young people.
Furthermore, there are many people born in the 90s that mock themselves for being the “four empties”.
These refer to an empty Alipay account, empty WeChat Pay account, empty debit card, and empty wallet.
This isn’t just self-mockery without factual basis.
According to a survey, 30% of people born in the 90s are part of the “moonlight group” ..
..  that have no money left over for saving each month.
The majority of their income goes towards consumption spending, ..
.. of which there is no lack of high-end consumption, including tech products, luxury items, etc.
From the outside, these spending habits seem to show that young people tend to have glamorous lives.
But when you take a deeper look, many of them have no savings on hand.
High spending or spending future money in pursuit of a refined lifestyle has made them poor.
These people are what is referred to as “refined but poor”.
The older generation of Chinese people are generally opposed to this type of consumer behavior.
They believe that this type of consumer behavior is like eating next year’s grain this year.
They believe that it lowers an individual’s ability to withstand risk.
But young people have many different thoughts on this.
Some believe that young people should enjoy being young and not worry necessarily.
Others believe that the yield from savings is too low.
They think that money saved in the bank will depreciate, so it is more worthwhile just to spend it.
Others believe that they should invest in themselves when they’re young, ..
.. and that plans for saving can be pushed back a few years.
Both sides stand by their arguments, and if no one is causing harm to society, we have no need to be overly judgmental.
Yet there are other social phenomena relating to the “refined but poor” that are worth looking at.
Some people pursuing the “refined but poor” lifestyle spend beyond their means on credit, producing serious consequences.
This happens quite frequently.
For instance, many college students take out online loans to buy expensive electronics or designer clothes.
They aren’t able to repay the loans, ..
.. and only communicate this to their parents when their job search upon graduation is affected due to their damaged credit.
In some cases, they commit suicide because they exceeded the family’s financial means.
With these tragedies, we have to be wary. How should we define reasonable desires and healthy consumer behavior?
In recent years, more and more people have begun to criticize the “trap of consumerism”.
This is their reflection upon overconsumption, and is also a type of exploration and seeking.
Perhaps one day, we can find a balance between enjoying life reasonably and withstanding unknown risks.
